question: An operations manager on a Pro plan is working within a single Project whose uploaded reference files are approaching the context limit. The manager wants Claude to keep giving high-quality answers grounded in that large body of documents without manually trimming the file set. What underlying capability does the Project rely on to handle this?
options: A) Research mode replaces the uploaded files with live web search results, automatically expanding project context without manual trimming.
B) An artifact compresses all uploaded files into a summarized attachment, expanding project capacity while preserving response quality.
C) Retrieval Augmented Generation automatically expands project capacity by retrieving relevant chunks, preserving quality.
D) A downgrade to a smaller model uses a reduced context window per document, allowing more reference files within the same overall limit.
correct_answers: C) Retrieval Augmented Generation automatically expands project capacity by retrieving relevant chunks, preserving quality.
explanations: Incorrect. Research mode is a separate web-search capability; it does not tap into the project's uploaded document base or automatically replace files to expand context.

Incorrect. Artifacts are for displaying generated content like code or documents; there is no artifact-based compression or summarization mechanism for uploaded reference files. Capacity expansion is handled by RAG.

Correct. Projects use Retrieval Augmented Generation to automatically retrieve relevant chunks from uploaded files, expanding effective context capacity while maintaining answer quality without manual trimming.

Incorrect. Downgrading to a smaller model changes generation cost and speed, not the way a project handles its uploaded knowledge base; it does not reduce per-document context usage to fit more files.
